title: From nine kids in a Rowlett living room to 59 young rockers: the Kids Who Rock story
excerpt: The Rowlett-born music nonprofit teaches kids to form bands and write their own songs, and its students have been singing for local seniors since 2016.
coverAlt: Dozens of smiling Kids Who Rock and Chicks Who Rock campers and volunteers pose together in a gym in front of colorful balloons.
credit: Kids Who Rock and Chicks Who Rock campers and volunteers, summer 2026.
body:
Eleven years ago, Patty Allen-Driver had an idea: give kids real instruments, put them in a band together and let them write their own song over the summer. Kids Who Rock started right here in Rowlett with nine students. Its very first camps were held in her own living room.

This past summer, 59 students took part. Together they write 10 to 11 original songs every year.

Kids Who Rock is now a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and it offers scholarships so that students who qualify can join no matter what their family can afford. It has also grown well beyond summer camp. Students get chances to shine on stage around town, and Kids Who Rock runs an after-school Theater Club at Harmony Science Academy.

Some of the program's most meaningful performances happen far from any big stage. Since 2016, in the months after the tornado that struck Rowlett, Kids Who Rock students have been singing at local senior living communities, bringing comfort, warmth and plenty of smiles to the residents.

"From 2 to 92, we want to make a difference in people's lives," Patty says.

So the next time you see a group of young musicians performing around Rowlett, at a community event or in a senior living community, there's a good chance they're Kids Who Rock. Cheer a little louder. They've earned it.
